StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterBlockGained.issue: The hook, the guards, the props and the dealer are all right -- amount <= 0 and creature == base.Owner (JuggernautPower.cs:19 vs powers.py:781), and CreatureCmd.Damage(target, base.Amount, ValueProp.Unpowered, base.Owner) (:26) vs DamageCmd.deal(..., self.amount, dealer=self.owner, props=DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED) (:791-794), where NON_CARD_UNPOWERED is UNPOWERED alone (valueprops.py:42) and so is BLOCKABLE, matching C# omitting Unblockable. cmds.py:150 fires the hook after the block is actually added, matching AfterBlockGained. THE GAP is the TARGET PICK -- see the RNG guard. Recorded here too because the observable is which enemy takes the damage, which is player-visible and conformance-visible, not just a stream position.

guards.issue: WRONG RNG STREAM. combat._rng is the SHARED unseeded random.Random (combat.py:88), NOT the per-purpose accessor object -- that is combat.combat_rng, built one line later at combat.py:94, whose seven named accessors (combat_rng.py:17-25: shuffle, monster_ai, card_gen, card_selection, targets, energy, potion_gen) are GameRandomAdapters over the matching RunRngSet streams in a parity run. This is the sixth and seventh power unit in this stream with the same defect -- power/aggression (main report section 4 item 8), then power/hello_world, power/entropy, power/stampede and power/confused in half A -- so it is systematic, not incidental, and it is proposed as its own PROMPT.md bug class in .superpowers/sdd/content-power-report-a.md section 7 item 11. LIVE under seed parity by construction: the draw comes off a different stream in a different order AND every later consumer of the shared rng is perturbed. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Juggernaut is the sharpest of the seven because the RIGHT accessor is used three lines away in the same engine for the same purpose: combat.py:546 picks an auto-play's target with combat_rng.targets.choice(living), citing CardCmd.cs:77's Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(HittableEnemies) -- and powers.py:792 picks Juggernaut's target with combat._rng.choice(living). Same C# stream, two different sim objects. Reachable: Juggernaut is a ported Ironclad card power and every block gain triggers it, so a Juggernaut run diverges on its first block in a multi-enemy fight.

guards.what: JuggernautPower.cs:21-22 CombatState.HittableEnemies and the empty check
guards.issue: The sim iterates combat.enemies filtered on not enemy.is_gone where C# uses CombatState.HittableEnemies, which additionally consults Hook.ShouldAllowHitting (Creature.cs:308-322), so the sim aims at creatures the game considers unhittable -- a mid-revival Illusion (powers.py:1572-1575) or a withered Decimillipede segment (powers.py:2354-2357). DORMANT: DamageCmd.deal re-checks should_allow_hitting at entry (cmds.py:51-52) and returns 0. Same finding and verdict as power/inferno's, power/constrict's, power/rolling_boulder's and power/the_bomb's HittableEnemies guards, per binding rule 3. The Count != 0 / `if not living: return` pair is present on both sides (JuggernautPower.cs:22 vs powers.py:787-788).

guards.what: Re-entrancy: Juggernaut's damage cannot itself grant block
guards.rationale: Neither side guards against on_block_gained re-entering, and neither needs to: the damage is dealt to an enemy and DamageCmd.deal grants no block. Note the sim also does NOT add the end-of-combat check that power/rolling_boulder and power/the_bomb add for their own sweeps -- so a Juggernaut hit that kills the last enemy leaves the combat un-ended until the surrounding code checks, which is hook_dispatch's G8 rather than this power's divergence.

guards.what: power/thorns cites this power as its reachability route
guards.rationale: audit/records/power/thorns.json's props guard names cards/juggernaut.py:38 -> powers.py:791-794 as the ported route to unpowered non-card damage with dealer = the player, which is what makes Thorns's missing IsPoweredAttack gate live. Confirmed from this end: the props really are NON_CARD_UNPOWERED and the dealer really is the player. Rule 3 agreement, recorded so the cross-reference is verifiable from both ends.
